title: Local presentability of accessible many-sorted monad algebras
statement:
Fix a universe $\mathcal U$. A category is locally presentable if it has $\mathcal U$-small Hom sets, all $\mathcal U$-small colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and, for some infinite regular cardinal $\kappa\in\mathcal U$, a $\mathcal U$-small family of $\kappa$-presentable objects generating every object under $\kappa$-filtered colimits. Here $\kappa$-filtered means every diagram with fewer than $\kappa$ morphisms has a cocone, and $\kappa$-presentable means its Hom functor preserves these colimits. Regular means a union of fewer than $\kappa$ sets of size less than $\kappa$ still has size less than $\kappa$.

Let $S$ be a $\mathcal U$-small set and let $\mathcal C_s$ be locally presentable categories. Their product $\mathcal C=\prod_{s\in S}\mathcal C_s$ is locally presentable. Let $T:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ be a functor with natural transformations $\eta:1\to T$ and $\mu:T^2\to T$ satisfying $\mu T\mu=\mu\mu T$ and $\mu T\eta=1=\mu\eta T$. Assume that $T$ preserves $\lambda$-filtered colimits for some infinite regular $\lambda\in\mathcal U$. The category of $T$-algebras is locally presentable, and hence complete and cocomplete. Its objects are pairs $(A,a)$ with $a:TA\to A$, $a\eta_A=1_A$ and $aT(a)=a\mu_A$; its morphisms $f:(A,a)\to(B,b)$ satisfy $fa=bT(f)$. Completeness and cocompleteness mean existence of every $\mathcal U$-small limit and colimit. No assertion that the algebra category has the same presentability cardinal as its base is made.
